one_line_contribution: A pre-registered ALFWorld measurement of what fraction of a procedural memory bank's task-type-specific advantage (and of its total gain over no-memory) is already held by a GEPA instruction optimized on the identical training episodes, identified by crossing instruction provenance against bank provenance in a two-task-set square rather than by ablating two containers filled from one undifferentiated pool.
closest_prior_work: ExpeL (arXiv 2308.10144), and the proposal concedes it. ExpeL's published ablation removes the prepended distilled-insight block and the retrieved-trajectory block separately, both built from the same training pool, and reports each single-container condition against the full system in ALFWorld. That is the same two-container redundancy question, on the same environment, in print since 2023; the proposal's own Related Work withdraws its 'nobody has reported the number' sentence because of it. What survives is narrow: provenance labelling of both containers, pairing, token matching, a reflective optimizer with a search budget in place of a fixed extraction routine, and confidence intervals. Worse, the authors state (risk 31, and under Verification limits) that they have not read ExpeL's ablation table because arXiv is unreachable from their node, and that 'if that table turns out to report a paired, token-matched retention ratio, the contribution reduces further.' A reviewer cannot grant novelty over a paper the proposers have not opened. Secondary threats they also concede: EvoAgentBench (arXiv 2607.05202) already puts GEPA (+1.2) and ReasoningBank (+3.6) on the same 528/267 training trajectories, publishing the qualitative headline; AutoManual (arXiv 2405.16247) already compiles ALFWorld experience into a single manual that replaces per-episode lookup, which makes prediction 6 a replication; and the crossover/held-out-provenance primitive itself is disclaimed.
strongest_objection: The primary threshold is not floor-adjusted, so a 'pass' would print a title the number does not support. The proposal computes a per-denominator headroom floor A_h - the value each ratio takes under literally zero absorption - and reports A_h(A) = 0.06-0.12, A_h(A0) = 0.16-0.22, A_h(A_all) = 0.04-0.08. It then applies the same flat point threshold, 'point estimate >= 0.5', to A and to the co-primary A0, and prices the floor only into the lower bound (via each ratio's own null). The consequence is arithmetic: A0 = 0.50 against a floor of 0.16-0.22 means roughly 0.28-0.34 of genuine absorption plus 0.2 of pure headroom, while A = 0.50 against a floor of 0.06-0.12 means 0.38-0.44 of genuine absorption. The two co-primaries are asked for materially different amounts of real content at the same nominal bar, and the abstract's sentence - 'at least half of the bank's task-type-specific advantage is absorbed' - is simply false on the A0 branch at its own floor. The design had the right bar and deleted it: v5.1's 'A - A_h >= 0.30' is explicitly withdrawn ('the bar is the truth table's conjunction, and nothing else'), which removes the only quantity that means the same thing across the three denominators. Compounding this, the correction bracket that is supposed to make the floor unnecessary is inert at both ends: best-of-w (row 14, n = 300) admittedly under-corrects and flatters the hypothesis, and the conservative end (Ladder T, row 4, n = 500, one optimizer seed, interpolated denominator) has SE(A_epi) ~ 0.30, i.e. an interval roughly as wide as the effect being bracketed. So the headroom defense reduces to a multiplicative compression model the authors themselves call 'a model, not a law' - and it is the wrong model here, because bank help is concentrated on specific hard games rather than distributed uniformly over the residual, which biases A upward in exactly the hypothesis's direction. Second head of the same objection: the design is near-certain not to reach its own headline. G3 is described as 'a deliberate coin flip', power for A's lower bound is 80/70/50% at Inner = 10/8/6pt, A0 is declared 'the harder of the two co-primaries', and endpoint E is declarable only when |g-hat| <= 0.68pt against a gated 5-15pt raw memory effect. Risk 34 concedes the modal outcome is the narrower T2 title. An area chair pricing the expected deliverable is pricing a gate-branch report or a partial-absorption paper whose headline number carries the floor contamination above.
what_would_fix_it: Four changes, in order of importance. (1) Restore a floor-adjusted confirmatory bar: require (A-hat - A_h)/(1 - A_h) >= 0.5 per denominator, computed from the directly measured levels (rows 1, 3, 16), so that the same nominal threshold means the same absorbed content for A, A0 and A_all, and so that an A0 pass at its 0.16-0.22 floor cannot be reported as 'at least half absorbed'. The matched-gap null on the lower bound is a good addition but it does not repair a point threshold that ignores the floor. (2) Re-tune the injection budget k at I_own. Right now k is 'fixed by a dev tuning run' under the hand-written scaffold and then HELD FIXED THROUGHOUT, including in the residual-gain cells; the track brief's own established prior is that injection volume, not content, is the causal lever (seven items harmful, three items not). Add I_own x B_own at a small k sweep so that g(I_own, B_own) is the bank's value at its best budget under that instruction, not at a budget tuned for a different one. (3) Stop pooling the numerator and denominator across directions before forming A. The confirmatory A is 'computed from direction-pooled numerator and denominator', which is a ratio of sums, not a mean of ratios: with T_A at Inner = 12pt and T_B at 4pt, the pooled A is essentially T_A's A, on two sets the proposal itself says are 'not exchangeable, by design'. Pre-specify a per-direction ratio and a fixed combination rule. (4) Execute the freeze-blocking obligation (1) and read ExpeL's, AutoManual's and AutoGuide's evaluation sections before submission rather than before the freeze, and cut the grid to what two A100s can actually run - A0, the residual gain g, the type-label rival I_type and R_raw at n = 1,200 - instead of twenty rows whose throughput assumption is transferred from another task.
missing_baseline: A per-instruction injection-budget control: B_own read at a k re-tuned under I_own, rather than at the single k tuned once on dev under the hand-written scaffold and then held fixed in every cell. This is not a nice-to-have - the research track's own headline prior result is that injection volume, not memory content, was the causal lever (cutting seven retrieved items to three eliminated the harm from the same bank), and the ALFWorld literature the proposal cites (arXiv 2604.27003, arXiv 2608.15008) says excessive retrieval harms sequential decision-making specifically. If the optimal k under a longer, procedure-bearing I_own is smaller than under I0*, then g(I_own, B_own) is depressed by context competition rather than by absorption, which pushes endpoint E toward passing and inflates A0 at the same time; the study would print T1 for a budget artifact. Secondary omission, and it is a Tier-0 omission by explicit refusal (risk 29): {C_own, C_oth} x {B_own, B_oth}, a non-GEPA prose summary of the same episodes. Without it a positive result licenses only 'a GEPA instruction built from these episodes absorbs the bank', not 'any instruction written from these episodes does' - and AutoManual (arXiv 2405.16247) makes the latter the likelier reading, which means the arm that would decide between them is the one that was cut.
preprint_collision: The check is methodologically the strongest part of the submission - 15 HuggingFace queries, 244 unique papers, by-id verification for 54 arXiv IDs, an EvoAgentBench PDF read in full with a committed SHA256, and a self-correction of a web snippet that had misreported ReasoningBank's Qwen gain as +7 when the PDF says +3.6 - and it is honest enough to withdraw its own novelty sentence over ExpeL. I could not name a recent preprint that already reports an absorbed share under provenance control. But it is not thin in method and strong in result; it is strong in method and unverified on the one axis that carries the claim, and three things make it a weakness rather than a neutral. First, the single freeze-blocking obligation - searching the contamination and data-attribution literatures for held-out-episode and data-provenance crossovers, i.e. 'is a learned artifact's benefit specific to the data it was built from' - is explicitly listed as UNRUN, and the whole identification claim is conditional on it. Crossover and leave-out-provenance designs are standard in transfer and contamination work, so this is likely to land at least partially, and the proposal pre-commits to reducing the contribution in print if it does. Second, the scan's recall is demonstrably poor where it matters: the two decisive same-environment precedents, AutoManual (arXiv 2405.16247) and AutoGuide (arXiv 2403.08978), were supplied by a reviewer rather than found by the scan, because it was weighted to the last six months - and those are exactly the papers that already establish, in ALFWorld, that episodic experience can be rewritten as instruction text and that a compiled manual competes with retrieval. Third, arXiv is unreachable from the node, so every 2026 ID rests on a single web-snippet channel and every 'confirmed absent from the paper' claim except EvoAgentBench's is asserted from abstracts - including, critically, the assertion that ExpeL's ablation does not already contain a paired retention ratio. A novelty argument whose load-bearing collision is a table the authors have not read is not established novelty.
